subject: Coord: emergency purge SLA, incremental backup purge schedule & subprocessor matrix (BrightMD)
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <security@brightmd.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Data retention and backup purge timelines — BrightMD

Hi Mateo,

We’re finalizing our DPA for BrightMD and need a clear statement of Redwood’s backup purge cadence, log retention exceptions for forensic use, and the emergency deletion workflow (customer-initiated). Attached is a redline of the DPA that flags a 14-day SLA for emergency purge of customer-identifiable test data, and a request to limit backup snapshots to a 30-day window for regulated datasets.

Specific asks:
- Confirm default backup retention and whether a 30-day backup window is supported per dataset or per account.
- Describe emergency purge flow (who executes, estimated time-to-complete, verification artifacts).
- Clarify log retention: we need an exception if forensic logs are retained >90 days and the justification/auditing controls.
- Provide subprocessor list for any cross-border transfers (we’re EU-anchored customers with US operations).

Attached: BrightMD_DPA_redline.docx (see comments on Sections 4 and 7).

Can you respond with a proposed timeline and any constraints by EOD Friday? Our legal team wants to move quickly.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Security, BrightMD
security@brightmd.com

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <security@brightmd.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Data retention and backup purge timelines — BrightMD

Hi Lena — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. I’m looping in Kimberly (legal) and Monica (Customer Ops) to cover DPA specifics and operational steps. High-level answers up front; more detail below and a draft purge schedule attached.

- Default backups: 90 days for full snapshots; incremental transaction-level backups for 7 days. We can propose a 30-day snapshot window for regulated datasets as a contractual option (requires reserved capacity for faster restores).
- Emergency purge: we propose a documented playbook — inbound request → identity verification → schedule purge (can be expedited) → purge execution → independent verification (audit log + signed confirmation). Typical expedited SLA is 72 hours; we can discuss a contractual 14-day SLA as requested, but need to clarify scope (snapshots vs. live indexes).
- Logs: 90 days by default; forensic retention up to 180 days with access controls and auditor logs. We can offer scoped exceptions with accountable roles and read-only forensic buckets.
- Subprocessors: I’ll attach the current matrix. Cross-border transfers are supported; we’ll surface third-party cloud providers and any managed partners.

Attachments: purge_plan_v1.xlsx

Next step: Kimberly, can you review the DPA redline and note where Redwood can accept the 14-day emergency purge and where we need to propose alternate language? Monica, please confirm operational constraints for 30-day snapshot retention and restore windows.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, Lena Ortiz <security@brightmd.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data retention and backup purge timelines — BrightMD

Thanks Mateo / Lena — quick legal take: we appreciate the specific asks. A few points for the DPA redline and proposed language:

1) Emergency purge SLA: Redwood can commit to a contractual acknowledgement and a 14-calendar-day completed purge for archived snapshots where customer provides authenticated request and required legal paperwork. For live indexes / active storage, we can complete deletion within 72 hours once identity verification is complete. We need to preserve a minimal audit trail confirming the action (timestamp, actor, job id) — that will be delivered as a signed deletion certificate.

2) Snapshot retention: default 90-day rolling full snapshots. Offering 30-day snapshot retention for regulated datasets is feasible as a configurable option, but operationally it requires a dedicated retention policy at provisioning and may affect restore windows (we’ll include SLA language that longer restores may be subject to a reserved-restore window of up to 48 hours to access cold snapshots).

3) Logs and forensic retention: we can classify logs into "operational" (30 days), "security" (90 days), and "forensic" (up to 180 days). For forensic logs kept >90 days we require a documented business justification and RBAC-limited storage with quarterly attestation.

4) Subprocessors & transfers: we will provide a current subprocessor matrix and note any subprocessor who may replicate data outside the EU. For regulated customers we offer contract-level commitments about subprocessors and can add notification requirements for new subprocessors that materially affect transfers.

I’ve added suggested DPA language as comments in the attached redline. If BrightMD needs a hard 14-day purge for all object types (snapshots + live) we should discuss pricing/reserved capacity and an escalation path for emergency deletion requests requiring legal hold checks.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Lena Ortiz <security@brightmd.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, BrightMD Legal <legal@brightmd.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 10:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Data retention and backup purge timelines — BrightMD

Thanks for the quick responses. A couple of clarifying questions before we sign:

- The 72-hour live-index purge SLA you mention is acceptable for active data. Our ask for 14 days is specifically for any archival snapshots that might still contain patient-test records — we want an end-to-end contractual guarantee for the customer-initiated purge of PII in backups. If you can commit to 14 days for snapshots that would meet our internal compliance review.

- For the forensic logs >90 days: what is the exact RBAC model and who at Redwood can approve the attestation? We need an escalation list for audit purposes.

- Finally, please confirm whether the emergency purge will remove encrypted object copies stored by third-party backup partners (subprocessors), or whether those are out of scope. If out of scope, we need notification and a subprocessor deletion SLA.

Lena
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <security@brightmd.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 14:00:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Data retention and backup purge timelines — BrightMD

Lena — agreed on next steps and proposed operational schedule below. Attaching purge_plan_v2.xlsx with the detailed steps.

Proposed operational commitments (summary):
- Snapshot purge cadence: configurable per account. Default: 90 days. Optional contractual add-on: 30-day snapshot window for regulated datasets (requires reserved capacity + $X/month).
- Emergency purge flow (customer-initiated):
  1) Customer submits secure request form + authenticated signer + legal affidavit (if required).
  2) Redwood Ops issues intake ticket; identity & legal review (up to 6 hours).
  3) Purge scheduled (expedited) and executed across live indexes and active object storage (target 72 hours).
  4) Snapshot purge: executed within 14 calendar days for archived snapshots if contractually agreed; we will attempt to isolate and remove snapshot copies earlier where feasible.
  5) Deliverable: signed deletion certificate and deletion job id + audit log extract.
- Logs: default retention tiers as Kimberly outlined. For >90 days forensic logs we require a business justification and an owner-level approval; approved owners are: Head of Security (Kimberly Park), Director of Ops (Monica Patel), and CTO (cc’d to exec when required).
- Subprocessors: the purge will include any Redwood-managed copies. For third-party subprocessor copies (e.g., long-term vaulting partners), we will 1) notify the customer immediately and 2) execute deletion under the subprocessor agreement terms (we can add a subprocessor deletion SLA in the DPA if needed).

Operational schedule: incremental purge job (non-disruptive) every Sunday 02:00 UTC; emergency purge window is separate and will be treated as high priority. We propose a March 1 canary purge on a non-production test dataset so BrightMD can validate proofs of deletion.

Attachments: purge_plan_v2.xlsx, link to deletion playbook in Drive: https://docs.google.com/document/d/drive-playbook-id

If this is acceptable, we’ll prepare a DPA amendment that includes the 14-day snapshot purge clause and a subprocessor deletion section for DocuSign.

Best,
Mateo
